Here we answer four practical questions. Who may do the inspection? Any licensed inspection station, and authorized stations display an official sign. How do you know one is due? When an inspection is needed, any licensed inspection station may perform it, and you can recognize an authorized station by the official sign it displays. To find out whether your next renewal needs an inspection at all, look at your registration renewal notice, which helps you tell. So pair them up: an even model year goes with even calendar years, and an odd model year goes with odd calendar years. The third trap is the fee. The cap is twelve dollars for most vehicles, but a motorcycle is capped at ten dollars, so the higher figure is wrong for a motorcycle. A two thousand seventeen model year vehicle that stays under one hundred fifty thousand miles is exempt from safety inspection through calendar year two thousand twenty-seven. The surprise is the renewal notice. Even though the renewal notice lists an inspection for such a vehicle, no inspection is needed. A certificate from a Missouri dealer is good for ninety days when the inspection was done within sixty days before the purchase date, so Tom's certificate is good for ninety days. A certificate a passing vehicle receives from a station is good for sixty days. We group the checklist into three parts.
